voyage.name: Prague Visitor Pass
voyage.content: The official city pass providing free public transport, a free ticket to ride on the vintage tram line 42 as well as free entry to various city attractions.

voyage.name: Prague Cool Pass
voyage.content: An unofficial pass available for 1, 2 or 3 days. Includes a bus city tour and a river cruise. Free entry to Prague Castle – St.Vitus Cathedral, Royal Palace, Golden Lane, St.George's Basilica. Free entry to Jewish Museum – synagogues and famous Old Jewish Cemetery (6 sites). In total, free entry to 50 attractions and discounts on over 30 attractions. Free guidebook with information about the attractions in 7 language

voyage.name: Prague City Pass
voyage.content: An unofficial pass providing free entry to various attractions in Prague within a 30 days period, various 25% discounts, sightseeing tours. Prague Castle – Old Royal Palace with Vladislav Hall, St. George‘s Basilica, Golden Lane with Daliborka Tower, St. Vitus Cathedral. The ticket is valid for 2 days from first entry. Jewish Museum in Prague – Maisel Synagogue, Spanish Synagogue, Pinkas Synagogue, Old Jewish Cemeter

voyage.name: National Gallery Gift Ticket
voyage.content: If you are an art lover and you are staying in Prague for a longer time, a dárková vstupenka (gift ticket) for National Gallery may save you money. The ticket is valid for a year and is valid in all exhibitions (both permanent and non-permanent) of National Gallery. Number of visits is not limited. A gift ticket for one person costs 650 Kč, for two persons 1000 Kč. For 240 Kč you can have one-person ticket valid for

voyage.name: Prague Spring
voyage.content: The most famous classical music festival in the Czech republic.

voyage.name: Signal Festival
voyage.content: A weekend in October, during which many historic buildings are lighted by spectacular video-mappings and many light-and-sound installations are set up at different places in the city centre, Vinohrady and Karlín.

voyage.name: Wine Boat
voyage.content: The 1-hour cruise includes a visit of Prague Venice river canal as well as wine tasting of local wines.

voyage.name: Prague Steam Boats
voyage.content: Offer one hour cruises, as well as cruises to the Zoo and full day cruises to Slapy water dam. If you have the time for a 3-hour dinner cruise, you will certainly enjoy viewing the city from the river, while savouring a great dinner.

voyage.name: Cruise Prague
voyage.content: Offers a wide range of regular and private cruises.

voyage.name: JazzBoat
voyage.content: Combines cruising and jazz concerts.

voyage.name: Football
voyage.content: The city's leading soccer team is SK Slavia Praha. They play in the First League, the top tier, and often qualify for European tournaments. They play at the 21,000 capacity Fortuna Arena, which is also the usual venue for international matches; it's 5 km southeast of the old city centre. The city's other First League sides are AC Sparta Prague (at Generali Arena, 1 km north of the centre) and Bohemians at Ďolíček sta

voyage.name: We Bike Prague
voyage.content: With We Bike Prague team you can easily discover the city of Prague and the area around. Very good quality bike to rent for you self guided trip in the city and multidays trip through the countryside. We Bike Prague is also specialized in long distance bike trip. Good bikes, panniers and maps can be rented for your cycling holiday in the Czech Republic.

voyage.name: BIKO Adventures Prague
voyage.content: BIKO offers mountain bike, road bike and outdoor activities off the beaten track in Prague and in the Czech Republic. From easy to advanced. High end bike rental: touring bikes, hardtail and full suspension MTB, road bikes, e-MTB.

voyage.name: Prague Tours Center
voyage.content: A free offer for the visitors of Prague: the Prague Tours Centre is offering free connection and charge up of your electric bikes and Segway PT. While connected, the devices are guarded by a supervisor and, in the meantime, you can take walk around Prague, visit a museum or your preferred restaurant. In the Prague Tours Centre the tourists have a possibility of depositing their bikes together with baggage which they

voyage.name: Running Tours Prague
voyage.content: Activity for those into running who want to explore the city and stay fit. It shows runners of all abilities around the city's musts while on the run. A traveling runner introduces the best of the Prague to their running shoes and feels just like a local runner. It usually takes 50–120 mins and 7–13 km. Your running in Prague is 100 percent customizable as to date, time, pace and distance.

voyage.name: Old Town Square
voyage.content: The center of the eventful history of Prague. The Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque buildings were preserved here. The Historical Centre, including most of the city’s major sites, became a UNESCO-listed site in 1992.

voyage.name: Týn Church
voyage.content: A very striking pure Gothic church on the outside, with a beautiful Baroque interior. The interior is free to visit with a suggested donation, but everyone except for worshippers at Mass must stay in the entryway area and no photos are allowed. You still have a very good view of most of the details of the interior from behind the rope, however, and it's well worth it for you to enter. Entry is via a building on Old T

voyage.name: Storch Building
voyage.content: Covered in murals.

voyage.name: Jan Hus Memorial
voyage.content: That striking man standing atop a patina-green metal mountain in the center of Old Town Square is not Jesus, though he resembles him. It's Jan Hus, the great Czech religious reformer whose Hussite movement caused as much, if not more, friction within the Christian community than Martin Luther. The statue was erected on the 500th anniversary of his death (6 July 1915). Hus preached in the Bethlehem Church in Old Town.

voyage.name: Astronomical Clock
voyage.content: The Astronomical Clock located on a side tower of the Old Town Hall (reasonably enough, on Old Town Square) is easy to find—just wait until a few minutes before the hour and look for a large group of tourists standing around waiting for something to happen! Still, Orloj is one of the most popular gathering places in Prague. The closer you are to the astronomical clock, the more astronomical the prices in restau

voyage.name: Municipal House
voyage.content: Nám. Republiky 5. The Obecní dům was built near the Powder Tower (a storage place for gunpowder and a major trade route entry into the city) on a site called King's Court where once a royal residence stood. In 1901, the Prague Civic Society made a proposal to city authorities to build a center for official and social Czech events. As happened so many other times in recent Prague history, the Czechs were trying to bal

voyage.name: Prague City Gallery
voyage.content: A museum of modern Czech arts divided between several sites most of which are in the old town. Its main building is the House of the Golden Ring at the Old Town Square featuring 20th century Czech art in a beautiful medieval edifice. 19th century Czech art is exhibited at the Troja Castle.

voyage.name: Speculum Alchemiae
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to the mysteries of alchemy, housed in a classified building dated from 980 AD in the center of the Jewish district, one of the only authentic buildings preserved after the massive redevelopment of the Old Town's Jewish Quarter during the 19th century. Only guided tours available in English or Czech. Tours include a history of alchemy, the role of the Kings in the alchemical development of Prague,

voyage.name: Convent of Saint Agnes
voyage.price: Admission: Full: 220 Kč, Reduced: 120 Kč, Family: 150 Kč
voyage.content: The Anezsky klaster is the first Early Gothic building in Prague (founded 1234) - something notable in a city filled with amazingly well-preserved examples of Gothic architecture such as St Vitus, the Charles Bridge and the Powder Tower. Over the years the complex's convent, chapels and several churches deteriorated and in some cases, were completely destroyed. After Habsburg emperor Josef II's religious reforms, the

voyage.name: Museum of Czech Cubism
voyage.price: Adult 150 Kč, senior or student 80 Kč (July 2020)
voyage.content: The Museum of Czech Cubism in the renovated House of the Black Madonna exhibits furniture suites, individual pieces, accessory furnishings and objects made of ceramic, glass and metals. It offers an overview of the foremost creative achievements of Czech Cubism’s key exponents. This unique Cubist building, designed by Josef Gočár, was built in 1911–1912.

voyage.name: Museum of Decorative Arts
voyage.content: This 17th century palazzo-style building houses examples of historical and contemporary crafts, as well as applied arts and design.

voyage.name: Church of the Holy Spirit
voyage.content: Baroque church

voyage.name: Pariska Street
voyage.content: Tree lined street with number of historic buildings, exclusive shopping and upmarket restaurants and hotels.

voyage.name: Rudolfinum
voyage.content: Neo-Renaissance auditorium, home of the Czech Philharmonic Orchestra. A statue of Antonin Dvořak is in the park in front of the building, whose front façade is being renovated as of August 2026.

voyage.name: Jaroslav Fragner Gallery
voyage.content: Contemporary architecture. You can find here profiles of influential people and groups, retrospective exhibitions, thematic exhibitions, recent movement in architecture. Gallery provides lectures, seminars and publishing, regarding central Prague. The JFG is a centre for architects, professional and general public, students of architecture and construction companies.

voyage.name: Sex Machines Museum
voyage.content: Humorous presentation of historic and present day sex toys and related installations. A visit takes about 60 to 90 minutes, and offers an initiation in the world of domestic and commercial pleasure engineering. No entry for persons under 18; not suitable for physically disabled people, due to the very steep stairs.

voyage.name: Lego Museum
voyage.content: A small museum dedicated to Lego bricks and their creations. Don't expect a history of the bricks, the museum is entirely focused on Lego constructions applied to the Czech context, with many monuments of Prague replicated as scale models in Lego. Most of the models on display are standard sets however, so the museum will be only worth its entrance fee for die hard Lego fans.

voyage.name: Powder Tower
voyage.content: One of the original city gates, which separates the Old Town from the New Town. The gate was used to store gunpowder in the 17th century, hence the name Powder Tower or Powder Gate.

voyage.name: Jewish Museum
voyage.content: This is not a single site but consists of four synagogues, the Old Jewish Cemetery and the Memorial Hall - entrance to all being covered by a single ticket. A combined ticket that includes the Old-New Synagogue can be obtained at a considerable extra cost but the interest of the building justifies it.

voyage.name: Maisel Synagogue
voyage.content: One of the historical monuments of the former Prague Jewish Ghetto. Nowadays the synagogue belongs to the Jewish Community of Prague and is administered by the Jewish Museum in Prague as a part of its expositions.

voyage.name: Spanish Synagogue
voyage.content: The Spanish Synagogue, so-called because Sephardic Jews expelled from Spain at the end of the 15th century built a previous synagogue on this site, is a wild combination of neo-Renaissance and Moorish-Spain style. Think the Alhambra crossed with a Victorian wallpaper store, with some Islamic geometric and floral flourishes thrown in for good measure. The predominant color is red, which lends a regal aura to the inter

voyage.name: Pinkas Synagogue
voyage.hours: Nov-Mar: 09:00-16:30. Apr-Oct: 09:00-18:00. Closed Sat (Jewish Sabbath) and Jewish holidays
voyage.content: Inside the front door of the Pinkas Synagogue, inscribed in tiny red and black letters on almost every square inch of wallspace are the names of 77,297 Jews who were killed in the war. This visual representation humanizes such a number, attaching names to the statistics. In larger type at the front of the synagogue are the names of the concentration camps in which they perished: Dachau, Mauthausen, Oswiecim (Auschwit

voyage.name: Old Jewish Cemetery
voyage.content: On the left wall before the entrance is a plaque detailing conservation efforts (which cost 1 million crowns per year). Over 20,000 people are buried in about twelve layers of graves, stacked to save space. Avigdor Kara is the earliest known person buried here - he was a poet who lived to tell about the 1389 pogrom. The reddish, grey and black tombstones are tilted at crazy angles, some covered with moss, some newly

voyage.name: Klausen Synagogue
voyage.content: The Klausen Synagogue is nowadays the largest synagogue in the former Prague Jewish ghetto and also a single example of an early Baroque synagogue in the area.

voyage.name: Ceremonial Hall
voyage.content: The last service to the deceased members of the Prague Jewish Community was held here.

voyage.name: Old-New Synagogue
voyage.content: The name sounds strange for a building from the 13th century but it was called 'New' to distinguish it from an even older synagogue. This was replaced by the Spanish Synagogue in the 17th century, when the Old-New Synagogue acquired its current name. It is rumoured to be the resting place of the famed Prague Golem.

voyage.name: Jewish Town Hall
voyage.content: Renaissance-style building

voyage.name: Stavovské divadlo
voyage.content: Oldest theatre building still standing in the city. Mozart's opera Don Giovanni was premiered here, with Mozart personally conducting, and Don Giovanni is still often in the repertoire, as are other operas, plays and ballets.

voyage.name: Thrill Park Prague
voyage.content: A haunted house with actors and VR zombie shooting.

voyage.name: FunCity Prague Arcade
voyage.content: Game mashines

voyage.name: City Game Prague
voyage.content: Interactive outdoor games and quizzes guided simply via WhatsApp messenger chat.

voyage.name: Hacker's Nest
voyage.content: Interactive co-op puzzle game requiring players to work together to save the world from destruction. Players solve puzzles and uncover mysteries in a race against time, attempting to defeat the doomsday plan from an Anonymous hacker. Minimum 2 players. No knowledge of hacker culture required, but minimal technical skills are helpful. Play time is 60 minutes. It is a relatively difficult game, not recommended for new

voyage.name: Grand Cafe Orient
voyage.address: Dům u Černé Matky Boží, Ovocny trh 19
voyage.content: Coffee, tea, cakes and sandwiches with free wi-fi between Namesti Republiky and the Old Town Square.

voyage.name: La Casa Blu
voyage.content: Spanish/Mexican food at good prices, close to Dlouha Trida tram stop. Free wi-fi internet. Service can be slow.

voyage.name: Lokál
voyage.content: A new member to famous Ambi restaurants group, this is the place, where traditional and modern blend together. While evoking Czech pubs from times years ago, everything is brand new. Beer (35 Kč) and food (100 - 200 Kč) is very good. Large non-smoking section in the back.

voyage.name: Restaurace Konvikt
voyage.content: Authentic local pub and restaurant

voyage.name: Dinitz Kosher Restaurant
voyage.content: Middle Eastern specials, in this Israeli restaurant offering Glatt kosher meals. The highlight is the Famous Sampler Menu, which consists of many tapas-style plates & mixed grilled meat on skewers.

voyage.name: V Kolkovně
voyage.content: Offers a combination of the tradition and uniqueness of the Pilsner Urquell brand and traditional Czech cuisine fused with modern gastronomy (French, German and International influences).

voyage.name: Kafka snob food
voyage.content: Good breakfast, nice place to sit at a street table with a coffee. Service can range from very good to poor depending who is working that day.

voyage.name: Indian Jewel
voyage.content: Very good Indian restaurant

voyage.name: Kavárna Obecní dům
voyage.content: Good selection of food in an interesting setting.

voyage.name: Bakeshop
voyage.content: A cafe with a large selection of warm drinks and cakes. Finding seating is not guaranteed during the busiest hours of the day, so check for seating before ordering unless you're planning to eat underway.

voyage.name: Five Rivers
voyage.content: Family friendly Indian restaurant, bar, cafe. Menu includes vegetarian and non vegetarian starter, main course and dessert. Free Wi-Fi, historical exhibit, no selfie ban.

voyage.name: Maitrea
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant with many vegan options. Wide range of food including both local and more international dishes.

voyage.name: Ambiante Pizza Nuova
voyage.content: An upscale place which does a very accurate rendition of Neapolitan pizza, but whose real selling point is the amazing play area for small and smallish kids.

voyage.name: Field
voyage.content: Michelin-starred fine-dining restaurant led by chef Radek Kašpárek. It focuses on modern European cuisine built around seasonal, locally sourced Czech ingredients.

voyage.name: La Dégustation Bohême Bourgeoise
voyage.content: Often voted as the best Czech restaurant, with price matching the quality. But if you have the cash, it's supposed to be a culinary experience as no other. Menu from 2200 Kč to over 4000 Kč with wine included. One of two restaurants in Prague with a Michelin star.

voyage.name: Marina Ristorante
voyage.content: Italian restaurant on a boat providing views across to lower town and the castle.

voyage.name: Robotic Bar
voyage.content: Cocktails from 140 Kč (May 2022) mixed by robots

voyage.name: Ice Pub
voyage.content: Drinks served in an ice-cold environment. You get a winter jacket there.

voyage.name: AghaRTA Jazz Centrum
voyage.content: AghaRTA is another well known jazz club, and organizer of the Prague Jazz Festival.

voyage.name: Al Capone's Cocktail Bar
voyage.price: Beer 25 Kč-70 Kč, cocktails 45 Kč-80 Kč
voyage.content: Al Capone's is a small and family-like bar, located in the very centre, with acceptable prices.

voyage.name: Chateau Rouge
voyage.content: Three-floor club in the old town. Plenty of tourists, including Americans and pub crawl groups, to be found any night of the week.

voyage.name: Karlovy lázně
voyage.content: This self-styled "biggest music club in Central Europe" is right next to Charles Bridge, with 5 floors of clubs each featuring a different style of music. It is frequented by Czech teenagers and German high school students. There are security guards at the door who search entering patrons. It is more often than not incredibly dirty and filled with very young males.

voyage.name: Music Club Zlatý Strom
voyage.content: Lively half dance club, half go-go club. Watch out for the bucket mojito cocktails for 599Kč!

voyage.name: U Zlatého Tygra
voyage.content: If you aren't easily scared off by smoke so thick you can touch and mean-looking Czechs that look like they would rather shake you than share a table, then this place is a must-stop. It is almost always crowded to standing capacity but if you stop by just before closing during the week, you can usually grab a table next to a local or knowledgeable expat and have some great Pilsner Urquell for 34 Kč a half liter, a pr

voyage.name: Restaurant Franze Kafky
voyage.content: Pleasant place to sit with a drink and people watch in the evening when the establishments on the old town square insist on food only customers.

voyage.name: Hotel U Tri Bubnu
voyage.content: Small 3-star hotel with unique rooms.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Hotel Prague
voyage.price: Bed and breakfast for 2 people is approximately €250, advance purchase packages are available for as low as €195 per night
voyage.content: On the river very close to the Charles Bridge. The Four Seasons is best known for having lowered the wall in front that protected it from the flood. But when dry it's as close as you get on the right bank to everything in Prague.

voyage.name: Hilton Prague Old Town
voyage.content: The hotel has 303 rooms, a restaurant on site, a wellness center with fitness equipment and a swimming pool. Room service is available.

voyage.name: Hotel Cerny Slon
voyage.content: Small, family run 4-star hotel a few meters from the Old Town Square. Rooms have private bathroom, satellite TV, IDD telephone, WiFi and safety deposit boxes.

voyage.name: Fairmont Golden Prague Hotel
voyage.content: One of the older Western hotels in Prague. Closed for renovation until late 2024, when it is planned to open as a 297 room 5* hotel.

voyage.name: Brewery Hotel - U Medvídků
voyage.content: On the site of an old brewery that is now a Czech Budweiser (Budvar) restaurant, the pension building houses a brewing museum and shop. It is also connected to a smaller bar that is open until 03:00. The rooms are clean and atmospheric. Ask for a room at the very top (#43 is a good pick) to avoid street/restaurant noise. Rates are seasonal but start from around 1550 Kč/2300 Kč/3100 Kč per night for singles/doubles/tr

voyage.name: The U Prince
voyage.content: Comfortable beds and beautiful marble bathrooms. The terrace bar has a view of the city and Old Town Square.

voyage.name: Clarion Hotel Prague Old Town
voyage.content: Near Old Town Square Modern equipment and services in a historic building dating back to 1930. Renovated rooms have internet, free WiFi in common areas.

voyage.name: Buddha-Bar Hotel Prague
voyage.content: Vibrant music and oriental aromas in the historic city centre of Prague.

voyage.name: Hotel Melantrich
voyage.content: Comfortably equipped fully en-suite rooms.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Praha
voyage.content: Luxury hotel in a historical building. Rooms with a view of the Apostolic Clock and the Old Town Square.

voyage.name: Hotel Rott
voyage.content: Comfortable accommodation in rooms styled in the late 19th century style, with modern amenities.

voyage.name: Hotel Paris
voyage.content: 86 room art nouveau hotel built in 1905.

voyage.name: Prague Castle
voyage.content: The former seat of the King and is now the seat of the Czech president. This is Prague's number one tourist attraction so expect huge crowds and possibly long lines, especially during high tourist season. Your best bet is to come early, as soon as the castle opens. Similar to other royal palaces, there is an hourly changing of the guard ceremony. At noon, the ceremony includes fanfare at a flag ceremony in the first

voyage.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
voyage.content: In the center of the castle and the most important cathedral in all of the Czech republic. The oldest parts of the cathedral are from the 14th century, but the cathedral was not completed in the Medieval period. The highest tower was completed in Renaissance and Baroque styles much later, as is clearly obvious. The Western portal and both Western towers are even younger, completed in the 19th and early 20th centuries

voyage.name: Old Royal Palace
voyage.content: The original seat of Czech rulers. Visitors first enter the Vladislav hall, the largest high-Gothic vaulted space in Central Europe. Other rooms include the Palace chapel and throne room. At the end of the exhibit is "The Story of Prague Castle" exhibit, which features artificats from the castle's past. The Old Royal Palace is occasionally closed to visitors, so it may be advisable to check this before visiting.

voyage.name: St. George's Basilica
voyage.content: The second oldest church in the castle and features a colorful Baroque facade. The interior is visibly older and is the burial place of the Premyslid family and the first Czech saint, Princess Ludmila.

voyage.name: St. George's Convent - National Gallery
voyage.content: One of several branches of the National Gallery is located inside this, the first convent in Bohemia. Today it houses the collection of Czech Mannerist and Baroque art.

voyage.name: The Golden Lane
voyage.content: During the reign of Rudolf II, goldsmiths lived in a lively alleyway filled with tiny workshops, which were also their residence, hence its name. Tiny, cobblestoned walkway filled with brightly-painted little houses, where modern man has a hard time standing with the low ceiling. (It's tough to realize just how tiny our pre-20th-century ancestors were until you go somewhere like this). Franz Kafka occupied No. 22 fro

voyage.name: The Daliborka
voyage.content: Built by Prince Vladislav in 1496, the tower at the far end of the castle is part of a new fortified wall. Its first prisoner was a recalcitrant knight named Dalibor who, according to legend, played his violin very sadly at the wall serenading the castle residents. Though, the thickness of the walls makes that legend a little unlikely. No one would have been able to hear him outside! Today the tower holds a small dis

voyage.name: Prague Castle Picture Gallery
voyage.content: Housed in the original castle stables. It contains Renaissance and Baroque art, including parts of the original collection of Rudolph II.

voyage.name: The Royal Garden
voyage.content: To the east/north-east of the palace is a large park. Aside from its own beauty, it has an excellent view of the east bank of the river. Entrance is free.

voyage.name: The State Rooms at Prague Castle
voyage.content: Open to the public two days of the year, as they are mostly used exclusively by the President. Contact the Castle Information office for more details.

voyage.name: Charles Bridge
voyage.content: connects the Old Town with Lesser Town. Commissioned by Czech king and Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV and constructed between 1357 and 1402, it is one of the most interesting historical stone bridges in Europe. It is 516 meters long with 16 arches. Baroque statues (a total of 30) began to be placed here in the 17th century. The best time to visit the bridge is in the quiet morning or in the evening at sunset, when one

voyage.name: The Lennon Wall
voyage.content: This historic graffiti wall, near a Venetian-like canal with water wheel and close to the Charles Bridge, used to be a source of irritation to the communist regime. a wall in Prague, Czechia. After the 1980 murder of John Lennon, a mural of John Lennon was painted by an unknown artist. As more people expanded upon it, the wall became a place for free expression of then communist Czechoslovakia. It is now an open-air

voyage.name: Child Jesus of Prague
voyage.content: This image of Christ, known also as the Holy Infant of Prague, is among the most widespread religious images in the world. The statue was brought from Spain in the 16th century and given to the Carmelites in 1628. It is 47 cm high and represents Jesus as a Child and King. The statue is carved out of wood and the surface is modeled in coloured wax. The entrance to the church is free of charge.

voyage.name: Petřín Hill
voyage.content: Due to a housing crunch, most young Czechs don't move out of their parents' house until they marry (sometimes long after!) This lack of privacy leads to some very public displays of affection – what you see on the metro or trams won't compare to what you’re likely to encounter on Petřín Hill. This hillside slopes down from the Castle and Strahov Monastery to Malá Strana and Malostranské náměstí metro station. It affo

voyage.name: Petřín Lookout Tower
voyage.price: Climbing the tower costs 220 Kč for a standard ticket or 150 Kč for discounts. Only ISIC cards are accepted for student discounts. Paid lift available (additional 150 Kč for adults) which takes you to the observation platform
voyage.content: A smaller version of the Eiffel Tower on the top of Petrin Hill overlooking Prague. The grounds near the tower contain a formal rose garden which is free to walk around. With a height of just under 60 m, it is about 1/5th scale of the Paris Eiffel tower, and was constructed shortly after its Parisian counterpart at the end of the 19th century. The tower has 2 viewing platforms, one about halfway, and one at the top.

voyage.name: Loreta
voyage.content: A beautiful Baroque convent in the Lesser Town.

voyage.name: Strahov Monastery
voyage.content: A monastery on the mountain. Worth a visit for both its picture gallery and its notable Renaissance library.

voyage.name: Franz Kafka Museum
voyage.content: Influences, life and works of the German language writer.

voyage.name: Wallenstein Palace
voyage.content: A nice Baroque palace with garden, it houses the Senate of the Czech Republic.

voyage.name: The Pedagogical Comenius Museum
voyage.content: A museum documenting the writings of the Czech Renaissance erudite, centering around the legacy of J.A. Comenius: traditions and challenges of the Czech culture and education. The story starts in the 9th century with early Christian literacy, detailing the role of Prague and its university in the European and international context. The Golden Age of humanism lays the foundations of modern pedagogy, with are explained

voyage.name: Lobkowicz Palace
voyage.content: Art museum near Prague Castle. Houses the original manuscript for Beethoven's famous 5th symphony, and many other interesting artifacts.

voyage.name: Museum Kampa
voyage.price: Adults 350 Kč, student/senior 190 Kč, child (under 6) free
voyage.content: A museum of modern Central European art.

voyage.name: National Gallery Prague - Old Masters
voyage.price: Combined entrance to both buildings 300 Kč (reductions 200 Kč), also other combined passes with other NGP branches
voyage.content: The Old Masters collection of the National Gallery, covering paintings from the 15th to 18th centuries, is divided between two mansions on Hradčanské Square, the Renaissance Schwarzenberg Palace and the Baroque Sternberg Palace.

voyage.name: U krále Brabantského
voyage.content: Tavern opened daily since 1375, recreating the ambient of 14th century Medieval Prague. Includes Medieval furniture and wall decorations, traditional food, and live entertainment by bards and sword fighters. Reservations recommended. An all-in evening package costs 1200 Kč.

voyage.name: U Zavesenyho Kafe
voyage.content: one of the very few restaurants in the tourist area of Prague with a quirky atmosphere that isn't excessively touristy. Offering food at reasonable prices and serving good, modest food. A great place to have lunch while exploring Hradčany and Petrin Park, it's conveniently located in the middle between these two tourist attractions.

voyage.name: Restaurant U Zlatých nůžek
voyage.content: offers a wide selection of Czech and international cuisine including first-class Moravian wines. Enjoy the unique atmosphere of calmness in the centre of Prague with its beautiful view of the Charles Bridge and enjoy the garden in front of the hotel during the summer season (May-October). The restaurant is suitable for family gatherings, company events and wedding celebrations.

voyage.name: El Centro
voyage.content: An excellent little restaurant located near the Charles Bridge, but tucked behind a couple of other buildings. It's a typical Spanish restaurant, has a very friendly atmosphere, good prices and isn't crowded. Also, it doesn't have any hidden charges such as service taxes which are common in Prague. English menus and takeout available.

voyage.name: Malostranska Pivnice
voyage.content: Traditional Czech cuisine. Sometimes you get a hand written bill with a service charge. Do not pay it. Tip only as much as you like.

voyage.name: Červená Sedma
voyage.content: Traditional food serving tourists, tables outside in pedestrian area.

voyage.name: LoVeg
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant serving local Czech dishes and international cuisine.

voyage.name: St. Martin
voyage.content: Cozy restaurant with Czech and American cuisine, next to the KGB Museum. Suitable for small groups or families with children. Reservations usually not necessary. Their home made ice tea is worth a visit.

voyage.name: Kampa Park Restaurant
voyage.content: High quality (and price) restaurant with excellent view of the Charles bridge and river.

voyage.name: Střelecký ostrov
voyage.content: Terrace provide a nice place to sit and drink and admire the view over the river.

voyage.name: U Glaubiců
voyage.content: Classic Czech pub, serving some of the best and cheapest beer in Malá Strana, normally one of the most expensive areas of the city.

voyage.name: U Malého Glena
voyage.content: American-owned bar with live jazz downstairs nightly. See video of this bar.

voyage.name: Dobrá trafika
voyage.content: Cosy cafe near Kampa with nice atmosphere, small garden and variety of small snacks and hot drinks. The cafe is located behind a newsstand (in Czech - trafika).

voyage.name: Cafe Club Ujezd
voyage.content: Kind of an odd bar in Mala Strana. Interesting art on the walls and ceilings. Even more interesting clientele. Cheap beer and a great place for groups.

voyage.name: EA Hotel Jeleni dvur
voyage.content: All 30 rooms are equipped with TV/SAT, high speed Internet connection, direct dial telephone and safe deposit box. Public PC desk with Internet access and printer is available at the reception. Some rooms offer a wonderful view of the historical parts of Prague. There is a parking lot in front of the hotel for those coming by car.

voyage.name: Golden Well Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with one of the most beautiful views in Prague and restaurant terrace leading directly to Prague Castle.

voyage.name: Hotel Questenberk
voyage.content: Romantic, baroque-style, 17th century hotel. Each of the Single, Double, Deluxe Double rooms and the three Royal apartments are originally furnished and equipped with TV, WiFi, phone, safe, and minibar.

voyage.name: Arpacay Hostel
voyage.content: Facilities include a kitchen, laundry and personal lockers. There's also a roof top terrace overlooking the city. Free breakfast, linens and internet access. There's no curfew.

voyage.name: The Charles Hotel
voyage.content: Josefska 1; Romantic 4-star hotel near to the Charles Bridge. Some rooms have antique wooden painted ceilings. Rooms are air-conditioned and equipped with safe, satellite tv, phone and minibar. Each room has private bathroom and free WiFi.

voyage.name: Hotel Sax
voyage.content: 4-star vintage design hotel. Every room or suite has an original appearance: design of the 1970s, furniture of the 1950s or 1960s.

voyage.name: Nerudova Apartment House
voyage.content: All apartments are fully furnished in standard way. A spacious living room includes a fully equipped kitchenette and a dinette. Maid service twice per week. Prices vary according to the season and type of apartment, from €50 for one bedroom apartment to €150 for large three bedroom apartment.

voyage.name: Pension Dietzenhofer
voyage.content: The main house is a cute green building dating from 1572. Rooms and suites there start from 1500 kc for a single. The flat, which sleeps up to 4, is a great value for backpackers at 1800 Kč/night. It has a fully equipped kitchen, dining room, bathroom, and is located on Karmelitska, a main thoroughfare in Lesser Town.

voyage.name: Alchymist Grand Hotel and Spa
voyage.content: Very luxurious, and rather expensive hotel located across the street from the U.S. Embassy.

voyage.name: Mandarin Oriental Prague
voyage.content: Part of the Mandarin Oriental chain. Very expensive.

voyage.name: Best Western Hotel Kampa
voyage.content: Authentically decorated hotel evokes the splendour of the 17th century and welcomes its guests with wonderful internal architecture and pleasant hotel comfort.

voyage.name: Prague Residences
voyage.content: Modern short term accommodation in fully serviced apartments.

voyage.name: Wenceslas Square
voyage.hours: The entire square is under reconstruction until 2027
voyage.content: Václavské náměstí is a wide boulevard running down from the National Museum and it's crammed with bars, restaurants and casinos. It is the heart of central Prague. All three metro lines cross there: line A and C cross at "Muzeum" station (upper part of boulevard next to National Museum), while lines A and B cross at "Můstek" station (middle to lower part of boulevard). Wenceslas Square and the surrounding area was an

voyage.name: National Museum
voyage.price: Adult 360 Kč, concession 260 Kč, kids under 15 free
voyage.content: Nature and history museum in the upper part of Wenceslas Square. The building was designed by prominent Czech neo-renaissance architect Josef Schulz in the years 1885 - 1891. In the older museum, there is an excellent permanent exhibition of various minerals including gems, as well as other interesting exhibitions including insects, fossils, animal skeletons, and stuffed animals from around the world. One of the best

voyage.name: Dancing House
voyage.content: It is the work of the twentieth century American architect Frank Gehry, and is said to be shaped like a man and a woman dancing; hence its former name "Fred and Ginger". Inside you can visit a gallery or go to the rooftop bar and restaurant and enjoy nice views of the river and castle.

voyage.name: Botanical Garden of the Charles University
voyage.content: Botanical garden of the Charles University with valuable outdoor exhibition and a collection of tropical plants in greenhouses.

voyage.name: Vyšehrad
voyage.content: Seat of Czech princes for centuries before Prague Castle was built. Site of St. Paul and Peter's Cathedral, and of the famous Vyšehrad cemetery known as 'Slavín', burial grounds of extraordinary Czechs. Don't forget to visit the casemate of Vyšehrad; they are picturesque, and you can see originals of some statues from Charles Bridge. From the ramparts of Vyšehrad, you'll have an excellent view of Prague castle, Vltav

voyage.name: Vyšehrad cemetery
voyage.content: Established in 1869 on the grounds of Vyšehrad Castle, it is the final resting place of many famous Czechs like artist Alphonse Mucha and writers Jan Neruda and Karel Čapek.

voyage.name: Basilica of St Peter and St Paul
voyage.content: A neo-Gothic church in Vyšehrad fortress.

voyage.name: Velvet Revolution Memorial
voyage.content: A simple brass plaque.

voyage.name: Jubilee Synagogue
voyage.content: Built in 1906, designed in Moorish Revival form with Art Nouveau decoration.

voyage.name: Museum of Communism
voyage.price: Adults 390 Kč, students with ID 310 Kč, seniors 340 Kč
voyage.content: An interesting museum that follows the history of communism in Czech Republic until its fall with the Velvet Revolution. The museum has several interesting communist propaganda artifacts, which are worth a look. Interesting exhibits on how communism changed Czechoslovakia, but skewed toward a particular view of history.

voyage.name: Mucha Museum
voyage.price: Adults 300 Kč, concessions 250 Kč, kids under 10 free
voyage.content: This museum is dedicated to the life and works of Alphonse Mucha, a leading artist in the Art Nouveau movement.

voyage.name: Head of Franz Kafka
voyage.content: A moving metallic sculpture behind the Quadrio mall.

voyage.name: Emauzy monastery
voyage.price: Adult 90 Kč, concessions 60 Kč, family 150 Kč
voyage.content: Founded in 1347 by Charles IV, Emauzy is a historic Benedictine abbey known for hosting Slavic liturgy. Destroyed by World War II bombing and famously restored in the 1960s with modern white concrete towers, it features original 14th-century Gothic cloisters and frescoes.

voyage.name: Máj Národní
voyage.content: A former shopping center, multiple floors now covered by arcade games and Marvel/DC-movie-heroes-related showcases. Top floor with city overview freely accessible. On the building facade are placed plane-butterfly art pieces.

voyage.name: National Theatre
voyage.content: The original National Theatre building. The interior of the building is very decorative, and a sight of its own. Sometimes hosts operas and ballets, but mostly plays in Czech language; English surtitles are often available. Students receive a 50% discount on tickets.

voyage.name: Mánes Gallery
voyage.content: A renowned functionalist exhibition space built between 1928 and 1930 on the Vltava Riverbank. Designed by Otakar Novotný, it serves as a major venue for modern and contemporary art, managed by the historic Mánes Association of Fine Artists, hosting exhibitions, social events, and offering iconic views near the Dancing House. Opening times and prices can be found on their website and may vary depending on the exhibit

voyage.name: Palladium
voyage.content: In the city centre, next to the main city (shopping) streets. It is among the most luxurious shopping centres. It's complex inside, so you'll need a while to walk through it. No cheap options to eat, unless you buy some food in Albert supermarket on the lowest floor (-2). On the top level (+2) are some moderate to expensive restaurants.

voyage.name: Dietní jídelna
voyage.content: Canteen specialising in healthy food. The dishes are presented on a plate which makes it easier to choose. Open M-F 11:00-14:00

voyage.name: Wokin
voyage.content: Stir-fries. It is possible to order on the app or kiosk and the food usually comes out quick.

voyage.name: Bageterie Boulevard
voyage.content: Czech fast-food chain that focuses on fresh, gourmet baguettes, soups, salads, and breakfast items.

voyage.name: Tian Tian Restaurant
voyage.content: Asian restaurant.

voyage.name: Zdravé žití U tří růží
voyage.content: Vegetarian

voyage.name: Střecha
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant

voyage.name: Plavecká Polévka
voyage.content: A bistro

voyage.name: Kung Fu Pure Chinese Pasta
voyage.content: Dumplings

voyage.name: Fresco Vento
voyage.content: Italian

voyage.name: Jáma³ Garden Pub
voyage.content: Good place for burgers. Free wi-fi.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Kmotra Kavárna
voyage.content: A great, inexpensive pizza place with a relaxed setting.

voyage.name: Pivovarský dům Benedikt- restaurace a pivotéka Praha
voyage.content: Microbrewery makes everything from a traditional Czech pilsner to beers flavored with sour cherries or banana.

voyage.name: Cafe Slavia
voyage.content: A coffee tastes even better when accompanied by stunning views of the Vltava and Prague Castle. Cafe Slavia is the perfect place to stop for a coffee or light meal during a day of sightseeing in Castle.

voyage.name: Café Louvre
voyage.content: Once frequented by Franz Kafka, this cafe is now a popular hotspot for a Prague locals. Their separate dining room offers French cuisine, for those looking for a different option than Czech food.

voyage.name: U Kroka
voyage.content: Charm restaurant with delicious food and reasonable price. Try the double colored beer!

voyage.name: Kantýna
voyage.content: Hip, market-style restaurant specializing in different cuts of meat and local side dishes. Most food is by weight: you grab a tray and have the cooks pile on whatever you'd like from their station. There are also items you can order off the menu: the burger and beef tartar are highlights. Outstanding flavors and fresh ingredients.

voyage.name: Restaurant Zvonice
voyage.price: Mains approximately 600 Kč, bottles of wine 800 Kč to 7000 Kč.
voyage.content: This romantic restaurant is spread over three levels high up in a Gothic bell tower. If you're lucky, you will get to eat dinner immediately beneath a huge bell.

voyage.name: Triton
voyage.content: Upscale restaurant, sea themed, located completely underground. Excellent food in an unusual decor, ideally suited for romantic dinners for two. Not suited for kids. The entrance is somewhat hard to find, ask in the bar on street level for directions.

voyage.name: Duplex
voyage.content: Situated in Wenceslas Square, this club pays US$5000 rent per day, and consequently charges an outrageous cover fee to teenage tourists who still think that Prague is the "wild" place it was in the early 1990s. This club does a good job of keeping the more pleasant clubs in Prague free from tourists who come for Prague's more disreputable aspects.

voyage.name: Lucerna Music Bar
voyage.content: Nice, but a little touristy; they play mostly 1980s music (with the accompanying music video on the big screen).

voyage.name: U Fleků
voyage.price: U Fleků 13° 99 Kč and spirits around 79 Kč
voyage.content: A restaurant that brews its own fantastic dark, sweet beer. It is the color of Coca-Cola with an alcohol content of 5.5% ABV, but its flavor is not overly strong. The servers will suggest a shot of local herb liqueur, Becherovka, but it won't be free. The atmosphere of this pub gets very rowdy as it is loaded with tourists from all over and bands play regularly. It's a lot of fun with a group.

voyage.name: Vinarna U Sudu
voyage.content: An incredible wine bar that doesn't look like much from the front, but if you look inside and go in the way back you'll find a huge underground maze of different areas each with their own unique music and vibe. Also nearby is the crossing point for all night trams.

voyage.name: Atlas Cabaret, Darling Cabaret, Hot Peppers, Club Empire, etc., around Wenceslas Square
voyage.content: The area around Wenceslas Square is popular with British stag groups, and there are numerous strip clubs on offer. Groups of young foreign men will be approached in the street by touts offering cheap drinks and women, and they will even trail you from pub to pub if it's a slow night and you haven't take them up on their offers. The strippers are full contact with touching allowed, while the girls in Atlas, Darlings a

voyage.name: Bike 7
voyage.content: In the evening, bars in port holes along the riverwalk open up. (Also a few on barges.) Popular with locals, they have lots of outdoor tables. Great place to people watch, and also see night fall over the castle on the hill.

voyage.name: Best Prague Hotel House
voyage.content: Apartments where can sleep up to four people with living room, bathroom and kitchen from 2450 Kč per night. Higher rates apply during peak season and for more than 2 guests.

voyage.name: Hotel Elite
voyage.content: Luxury 4-star hotel on the edge of Old Town and New Town. 78 rooms containing pieces of original antique furniture, A/C, private bathroom, IDD, pay TV, satellite, free WiFi, safety deposit box and a minibar, wellness, hotel garages.

voyage.name: Hotel Atlantic
voyage.content: A 3-star hotel located in the City Center on walking distance from all major historical sites. It offers 62 spacious, comfortable rooms, of which 3 have access for disabled people. Rooms are fitted with shower, WC, satellite TV, direct-dial (IDD) telephone, wifi and safety deposit box.

voyage.name: Hotel Best Western Meteor Plaza
voyage.content: 4-star hotel just outside the Old Town gate, within walking distance of much of the city centre. Amenities include air conditioning, shower and/or bath, WC, hair dryer, satellite/pay TV, IDD telephone, personal safe, coffee/tea maker, and mini-bar. Rate includes breakfast and wireless Internet access.

voyage.name: Miss Sophie's
voyage.price: Prices start at 420 Kč for a shared room and 1,630 Kč for a private room.
voyage.content: This designer boutique hotel/hostel is the perfect destination for a quiet getaway in the heart of Prague's New Town. Miss Sophie's offers private hotel rooms, apartments, and shared rooms. Gourmet breakfast is prepared and served daily in brick cellar basement.

voyage.name: Mosaic House
voyage.content: A unique blend of 4-star hotel and hostel. Downstairs, the restaurant and bar have a wide variety of local and international food and drink options. It's a blend of style, ecofriendly features, fun, and culture for all ages. Prices range from 250 Kč for a shared room and 1,400 Kč for a private double. Modern, eco-friendly, and centrally located. From shared rooms to private rooms with terraces, all are beautifully de

voyage.name: Dahlia Inn
voyage.content: Family-run accommodation.

voyage.name: Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Luxury five-star hotel just off Wenceslas Square.

voyage.name: 987 Prague Hotel
voyage.content: For €1 more get free phone calls to Europe. Free internet.

voyage.name: Deminka Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Located in Prague city center, near the National Museum.

voyage.name: Hotel Merlin
voyage.content: Three-star accommodation in the center of Prague on the banks of the Vltava River, next to Dancing House near the metro station Karlovo náměstí

voyage.name: Apartments Emma
voyage.price: From 800 Kč for 2-person studio during low season. Rates are higher at peak times
voyage.content: Apartments from two to four people to rent near Vysehrad castle. Kitchen, internet and no curfew. The host is very helpful for information about public transport, attractions and night life.

voyage.name: Botel Racek
voyage.content: A hotel boat on the Vltava river offering rooms and suites, all with private bathroom, TV and phone. There's a Czech restaurant on board and you can enjoy drinks on the deck or in the bar. Botel Racek is ten minutes away from the city centre by tram and has private parking available. Singles, doubles, triples and quads. Prices vary depending on season, there are last minute offers.

voyage.name: Easy Housing
voyage.content: Hostel.

All three metro lines cross there: line A and C cross at "Muzeum" station (upper part of boulevard next to National Museum), while lines A and B cross at "Můstek" station (middle to lower part of boulevard). Wenceslas Square and the surrounding area was an
